solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Examine light tanker right near front

indicators.note: the letter for right is shifted from the end to sit close to the start of the word

parts.note: a bowser is a small mobile fuel or water tanker

explanation.surface: An inspector is told to look over a small tanker parked on the right near the front of a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowser is a small tanker (in Britain, a fuel truck at an airfield); 'near front' moves its final R to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: To look through or scan something casually is a synonym of examining it.

clue.text: Industrial region overlooking hard city to the north in country

indicators.note: overlooking in the sense of missing out, so a letter is left out

parts.note: the Ruhr is Germany's great industrial region
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the city's letters are turned round

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A geography note: an industrial zone above a city lies further north in the same country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' looks positional but means ignoring the H of RUHR; 'to the north' turns LA upwards to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated in the countryside, rather than a town, is described as rustic or rural.

clue.text: Caribbean prisoners detained in wrong state

parts.note: WI stands for West Indies, the Caribbean islands

indicators.note: the prisoners are held inside the word for wrong

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
cons are convicts

explanation.surface: Caribbean prisoners are being held in the wrong jurisdiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty US states, an example of the definition.

clue.text: One dumped in hearing from afar?

parts.note: a former partner who has been dumped is an ex
otic is the adjective for things relating to the ear and hearing

explanation.surface: Someone thrown over complains they were dumped within earshot, by someone from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: OTIC is the anatomical adjective for the ear; the surface makes 'in hearing' sound like a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something introduced from a distant foreign country is called foreign or outlandish, hence exotic.

clue.text: Queen enters museum facing hotel and gallery

indicators.note: the queen goes inside the museum's name

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The Queen visits a museum opposite a hotel and its gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum, written out in full as V and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed open porch along a house, a sense of gallery in architecture.

clue.text: It's essential to back convert with umbrella in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things are in a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to turn an umbrella inside out the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words CONVERT and UMBRELLA, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine runs down the back and is an indispensable part of it anatomically.

clue.text: Merchant in flap not working after payment devoid of note

indicators.note: after puts the flap piece behind the payment piece
devoid of means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: rent is a regular payment

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the word for working

parts.note: an aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft wing
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A merchant is in a flap because, after paying out, something has stopped working and no banknote remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' is an aircraft wing flap, not a panic; 'not working' means without the word on.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a trader who sells goods to the public, a kind of merchant.

clue.text: Famous denial given to old premier?

parts.note: no is a denial
Ted Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister was refused something, and wonders whether he was famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well known or celebrated is a synonym of being distinguished or famous.

clue.text: King soon touring school getting TV award? Not half

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for soon surrounds the rest

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: only half of the award's name is kept, the second half being dropped

parts.note: an Emmy is the American television award

explanation.surface: A king will soon tour a school that has won a TV award, though only half the honour.
explanation.walkthrough: GAM plus EM (half of EMMY) sits inside ANON. GAM, a school of whales, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the Greek king of Mycenae who led the expedition against Troy.

clue.text: A racist or ruffian held around middle of electoral count, maybe

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are held round another piece
a ruffian is rough and disorderly, so the letters are roughed up
the central letter of the word electoral is taken

explanation.surface: A racist thug is detained around the middle of an election count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffian' is an adjective-like anagram signal; the shuffled ARACISTOR wraps T, the middle letter of 'electoral'.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a nobleman, so he is one example of a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Slight alteration wife ignored in wood

indicators.note: the letter for wife is left out

parts.note: a tweak is a small adjustment

explanation.surface: A small change to a woodwork plan is made without the wife's say.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard tropical timber, an example of wood.

clue.text: Part of cleaning material producing complaint in front of old lift

indicators.note: in front of places the illness before the rest

parts.note: flu is an illness, a complaint
a lift is a ride in someone's car

explanation.surface: A cleaning product gives someone an illness in front of an old elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' means a ride in a car, not an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluoride is an ingredient added to toothpaste, the cleaning material for teeth.

clue.text: Truly how one might describe words allowing property transfer?

definitions.meaning: an emphatic word meaning really, certainly

definitions.text: how one might describe words allowing property transfer?
definitions.meaning: the wording that conveys property is written within a legal deed

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN DEED describes the wording of a conveyancing document.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an intensifier meaning really or certainly; split, it locates words inside a deed.

clue.text: Foundation? One's missing singer

indicators.note: missing says that letter is gone

parts.note: a basis is a foundation
I is the Roman numeral for one; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A foundation is lacking because one singer has gone absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a man with the lowest singing voice, so he is a type of singer.

clue.text: One defending most of rationale in a job

indicators.note: the shortened reasoning sits inside the word for job

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: logic is reasoning, a rationale

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for most of the reasoning behind a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist is someone who argues in support of a cause, a defender.

clue.text: Wine that's mature, not soft drink

indicators.note: not removes the soft letter

parts.note: ripe means mature
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a sling is a cocktail, as in Singapore sling

explanation.surface: A wine said to be mature but not a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape and the wine made from it, an example of wine.

clue.text: Male in Spanish city with Asian discussed foodstuff

indicators.note: the male letter is placed in the city's name

parts.note: Leon is a city in northern Spain

indicators.note: discussed says the word for the Asian is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a Kurd is from Kurdistan in western Asia

explanation.surface: A man in a Spanish city talks with someone from Asia about a foodstuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon curd is a sweet spread of lemon, sugar, butter and eggs, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon curd is a sweet preserve spread on bread, an example of a foodstuff.

clue.text: One often exhibited steel product lately in West perhaps

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star
steel in the sense of resolve or courage, grit

indicators.note: lately points to the last letter of the word product

explanation.surface: A steel product turns up recently in the West, often put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West perhaps' is Mae West; René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Magritte is a painter whose works hang in galleries, so he is often on show.

clue.text: Ruin left after two rivers cover top of walkway

indicators.note: after places the letter for left at the end
the first river covers, so encloses, a letter

parts.note: the Don is an English river

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of the word walkway

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A ruined path: left after two rivers flood over the top of a walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a collapse or loss of status, the same as someone's ruin.

clue.text: Animal hunted in sunless capital

indicators.note: sunless means with no S, the abbreviation for sun

parts.note: Minsk is the capital of Belarus

explanation.surface: An animal is hunted in a gloomy capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The mink is a small weasel-like creature trapped and hunted for its fur.

clue.text: Retired writer cut relative

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A retired writer cuts off a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is the son of your brother or sister, a family relation.

clue.text: Lace is caught in entrance

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed in the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance
ct is a scorecard abbreviation for caught in cricket

explanation.surface: A piece of lace has been caught in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace' is a verb: to spike a drink, i.e. tamper with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace a drink is to tamper with it by adding alcohol or a drug, to adulterate it.

clue.text: Flower turning up in diagram, a tulip

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tulip in a botanical diagram is shown turned upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows: here the River Tamar, on the Devon-Cornwall border. 'in' marks the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is often a river, something that flows, and the Tamar is one.

clue.text: Director once entertained by foreign banker, florid sort?

indicators.note: the director is held inside the river's name

parts.note: the Oder is a river in Europe; a river has banks
David Lean was the late British film director

explanation.surface: A former film director is hosted by a foreign banker of rather flamboyant type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword code for a river, here the German-Polish Oder.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a showy flowering shrub, so a flowery or blooming kind of plant.

clue.text: Achievement by one on course keen largely to retain lecturer

indicators.note: the shortened word keeps a letter inside
largely means most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: A student keen on achieving largely holds on to a lecturer during the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course: an eagle is two under par on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: On the golf course, a score of two strokes under par for a hole is a notable feat.

clue.text: Gandhi? Fellow followed by liberal mass around India

indicators.note: the letters go round the one for India
followed by sets the next letters after the first

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about Gandhi: a liberal fellow followed by masses around India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gandhi' is the 1982 Richard Attenborough biopic, not the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandhi is the title of an Oscar-winning 1982 movie, an example of a motion picture.

clue.text: Unionist in comradely society, obscure figure hugging good official near pack?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the society's name

parts.note: Toc H is a Christian fellowship founded after the First World War

indicators.note: hugging means enclosing a letter

parts.note: Jude is the hero of Hardy's novel Jude the Obscure

explanation.surface: A Unionist in a fraternal society, an obscure figure, embraces a good official near the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Toc H is a British Christian fellowship; in rugby the touch judge runs the sideline, near the scrum's pack of forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, the touchline official flags the ball out of play near where the forwards' pack plays.

clue.text: Luxury fish? Leader in theatre keeps tons

indicators.note: keeps in the sense of holding onto something, so the surgeon word holds the tons letter within it

parts.note: a surgeon leads in the operating theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre lead keeps tons of expensive fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is an operating theatre, not a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is the fish whose roe is caviar, the epitome of a luxury food.

clue.text: Ingenuity encapsulating top broadcasting figure close to expensive gismo

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: wit means cleverness or ingenuity
DG is the Director-General, head of the BBC

indicators.note: close to takes the last letter of the word expensive

explanation.surface: Clever thinking about a top broadcaster leads to an expensive gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The DG is the Director-General of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: A widget is a small mechanical device or gadget, a synonym of gizmo.
